analysis.title: European Rates – The Morning Call: The Week Ahead: 26-30 October
key_insights: Week-ahead key events: UK Autumn Budget (Wed), FOMC/BoC/RBNZ (Wed), ECB (Thu), BOJ (Fri). US data: conference board consumer confidence and durable goods (Tue), Q3 GDP, initial jobless claims and core PCE (Thu), Chicago PMI (Fri). Euro area Q3 GDP and HICP flashes for Germany, France, Spain and Italy are due Friday.

Citi expects the ECB to refrain from talking about France this week but says it cannot be avoided. Unanchored OAT valuations likely mean careful wording and a reminder of conditional backstops, but no plans for direct intervention, partly because it might not work.
OAT-Bund widening began by tracking a higher ECB hike premium. The causality then switched, with OAT-Bund widening capping the ECB premium and causing it to decouple from natural gas prices.
Citi says EGB spread volatility may be at a tipping point where it does not just limit further ECB hikes but prevents them.
Citi recommends receiving Dec26 ECB €STR, currently at 2.63%.

In sterling swap spread analysis, Citi builds curves with no exposure to the 5y rate to reduce the conditional negative skew of long-end steepeners. The 5y5y/10y5y and 20y5y/25y5y curves have stood out since March for limiting exposure to sharp front-end selloffs while keeping exposure to gradual rallies.

French SSAs have underperformed other major SSAs, and even OATs, in H2 26. SSA bid-ask spreads have widened for all major issuers as EUR rates sold off, and for French agencies they widened the most. Their RV versus OATs has improved on paper, but the wide bid-ask spreads raise the question of what it costs investors to transact in them.

Supply this week: EU up to €7bn, Belgium €2-2.8bn, Germany €10.5bn (Schatz and 10yr Bund), Italy about €11.25bn, Finland €0.4bn. USTs total $213bn across 2yr, 5yr, 7yr and 2yr FRN. Gilts total £5.5bn.
Weekly estimated DV01 of issuance across the auction calendar totals $106.5mn per bp.
Friday rating actions: Moody's on EFSF and DBRS on Spain.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Citi economists expect the ECB to hold at 2.50% on Thursday, as widely expected, with a meeting-by-meeting approach.
Citi's base case is for ECB hikes in December and March 2027, with inflation outlook worse since September but little evidence of second-round effects.

macro_indicators.reading: Hold this week, 25bp hike in December
macro_indicators.interpretation: Citi economists' base case is a Fed hold this week and a 25bp hike in December. A sustained equity sell-off could make September's 25bp hike the first and last of the cycle.
Citi expects the BoJ to hold, with Board member Takata again proposing a hike. Base case is quarterly hikes through mid-next year, the next in December, ending at a 2% terminal rate.
Current pricing level Citi recommends receiving.

trade_ideas.rationale: OAT-Bund widening now caps the ECB hike premium, and EGB spread volatility may prevent further hikes.

risk_factors: Unanchored OAT valuations and French spread volatility could limit or prevent ECB hikes.
A sustained equity sell-off could make the Fed's September hike the last of the cycle.
Wide bid-ask spreads in French SSAs raise transaction costs and limit execution.
charts_described: Figure 2 plots 10yr OAT-Bund (constant maturity, bp) against €STR 1y1y (%) from Mar26 to Oct26, and Citi says causality has likely switched from ECB premium pushing up OAT-Bunds to OAT-Bunds capping ECB premium.
Figure 3 plots €STR 1y1y against European natural gas (EUR/MWh) from Jul26 to Oct26, and Citi describes ECB pricing as at a stalemate between energy price gains and OAT volatility.
vol_and_positioning: Citi says EGB spread volatility, specifically OAT-Bund, may be at a tipping point where it prevents further ECB hikes.
ECB pricing has reached a stalemate between further gains in energy prices and OAT volatility.
